options: isolate the circuit, lock it off and prove it dead with a tester

wet the hands to improve grip

questions.explanation: Efficiency = output / (output + losses) = 9600 / 10000 x 100 = 96%.

questions.explanation: Both half-cycles are used, giving two output pulses per input cycle: 2 x 50 = 100 Hz (half-wave gives 50 Hz).

A 6-pole, 50 Hz three-phase induction motor runs at 960 rev/min. Its percentage slip is

questions.stem: A d.c. series motor must never be started without a load because
options: its speed rises to a dangerously high value
questions.explanation: With no load the series field weakens as current falls, so speed rises without limit (runaway).

questions.stem: The Kainji and Jebba power stations on the River Niger generate electricity by
questions.explanation: Both are hydro-electric stations using the energy of water held behind dams.

questions.stem: Discrimination between protective devices in an installation means that
options: only the device nearest the fault operates, leaving the rest of the installation supplied
all fuses blow together to give maximum safety
circuit breakers are used instead of fuses
the main switch trips before any final circuit fuse
questions.explanation: Correct grading ensures the smallest device closest to the fault clears it first.

questions.stem: The main reason for earthing the metal casing of an electric iron is to
options: provide a low-resistance path for fault current so the fuse blows or breaker trips
questions.explanation: If a live wire touches the case, the earth path lets a large current flow to operate the protection, preventing shock.

questions.stem: The instrument used to measure the insulation resistance of an installation is the
questions.explanation: A megger applies a high d.c. test voltage (e.g. 500 V) and reads megohms; low readings show insulation breakdown.

questions.stem: For the same length, why is 2.5 mm^2 cable used for socket-outlet circuits while 1.5 mm^2 cable is used for lighting circuits?
options: Socket circuits carry larger currents, so a larger cross-section is needed to limit heating and voltage drop
Lighting circuits work at a higher voltage
Thinner cable has a lower resistance
questions.explanation: Current-carrying capacity rises with cross-sectional area; resistance falls as area increases.

questions.stem: Electricity is transmitted over long distances in Nigeria at 132 kV and 330 kV mainly because
options: high voltage is safer for people near the lines
transformers only work at high voltage
high voltage means low current, reducing I^2R losses and conductor size
questions.explanation: For a given power, raising voltage lowers current, so line losses (I^2R) and conductor cost fall.

questions.explanation: A short or earth fault draws a large current that trips protection; an open circuit would simply not heat.

questions.stem:
(a) State Kirchhoff's voltage law. [2 marks]
(b) A 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance in series with a 2 ohm resistor, and a 6 V battery of negligible internal resistance in series with a 3 ohm resistor, are connected in parallel (positive terminals joined) across a 6 ohm load. Using Kirchhoff's laws, calculate (i) the voltage across the load (ii) the current in each battery (iii) the current in the load. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) In any closed loop, the algebraic sum of the e.m.f.s equals the algebraic sum of the p.d.s (IR drops)
2 marks: (b) Correct equations, e.g. 12 = 2I1 + 6(I1 + I2) and 6 = 3I2 + 6(I1 + I2), or the nodal equation (12 - V)/2 + (6 - V)/3 = V/6
2 marks: (b)(i) Solving: V = 8 V across the load
2 marks: (b)(ii) I1 = (12 - 8)/2 = 2 A from the 12 V battery; I2 = (6 - 8)/3 = -0.67 A, i.e. 0.67 A flows INTO the 6 V battery (it is being charged)
2 marks: (b)(iii) Load current = 8/6 = 1.33 A (check: 2 - 0.67 = 1.33 A)
questions.explanation: KVL: sum of e.m.f.s = sum of IR drops round any loop. Nodal: (12 - V)/2 + (6 - V)/3 = V/6 gives V = 8.000000000000002 V; I1 = 1.9999999999999991 A, I2 = -0.67 A (the 6 V battery is charged at 0.67 A), load current = 1.33 A.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the principle of operation of a transformer. [3 marks]
(b) A 10 kVA, 2200/220 V single-phase transformer has 500 turns on its primary. Assuming it is ideal, calculate (i) the number of secondary turns (ii) the full-load primary and secondary currents. [4 marks]
(c) State three methods of cooling transformers. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Alternating current in the primary sets up an alternating flux in the core (1); the flux links the secondary winding (1); by mutual induction an e.m.f. is induced in the secondary, proportional to its number of turns (1)
2 marks: (b)(i) Ns = Np x Vs/Vp = 500 x 220/2200 = 50 turns
2 marks: (b)(ii) Ip = 10000/2200 = 4.55 A (1); Is = 10000/220 = 45.45 A (1)
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: natural air cooling (AN); air blast/forced air (AF); oil immersed natural cooling (ONAN); oil immersed with forced air (ONAF); forced oil circulation (OFAF); water cooling of oil (OFW)
questions.explanation: An alternating primary current produces an alternating flux that links the secondary and induces an e.m.f. by mutual induction. Ns = 50; Ip = 4.55 A; Is = 45.45 A. Cooling: natural air, air blast, oil natural, oil with forced air or forced oil.

questions.stem:
A series circuit of resistance 40 ohms, inductance 0.2 H and capacitance 50 microfarads is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz supply.
(a) Calculate (i) the inductive reactance (ii) the capacitive reactance (iii) the impedance (iv) the current. [6 marks]
(b) Calculate the resonant frequency of the circuit. [2 marks]
(c) State two conditions that exist in a series circuit at resonance. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) X_L = 2 x pi x f x L = 2 x 3.142 x 50 x 0.2 = 62.8 ohms
1 mark: (a)(ii) X_C = 1/(2 x pi x f x C) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x 50 x 50 x 10^-6) = 63.7 ohms
2 marks: (a)(iii) Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2) = sqrt(40^2 + -0.83^2) = 40.01 ohms
2 marks: (a)(iv) I = V/Z = 220/40.01 = 5.5 A
2 marks: (b) f0 = 1/(2 x pi x sqrt(LC)) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x sqrt(0.2 x 50 x 10^-6)) = 50.3 Hz
2 marks: (c) Any two, 1 mark each: X_L = X_C; impedance is minimum and equal to R; current is maximum; current is in phase with the supply voltage (unity power factor)
questions.explanation: X_L = 62.8 ohms, X_C = 63.7 ohms, Z = 40.01 ohms (almost purely resistive), I = 5.5 A. f0 = 50.3 Hz, very close to 50 Hz, which is why the circuit is nearly resonant. At resonance X_L = X_C, Z = R (minimum), current is maximum and in phase with V.

questions.stem:
(a) State two advantages and two disadvantages of the moving-coil instrument. [4 marks]
(b) A moving-coil instrument has a resistance of 50 ohms and gives full-scale deflection with 2 mA. Calculate the resistance required to convert it into (i) a voltmeter reading up to 100 V (ii) an ammeter reading up to 5 A, and state how each resistance is connected. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Advantages, any two: uniform (linear) scale; high accuracy and sensitivity; low power consumption; not affected by stray fields; effective eddy-current damping
2 marks: (a) Disadvantages, any two: measures d.c. only (needs rectifier for a.c.); more expensive; delicate hairsprings/coil easily damaged by overload
3 marks: (b)(i) Multiplier R = V/Im - Rm = 100/0.002 - 50 = 49950 ohms (2), connected in series with the coil (1)
3 marks: (b)(ii) Shunt R = Im Rm/(I - Im) = 0.002 x 50/4.998 = 0.02 ohms (2), connected in parallel with the coil (1)
questions.explanation: Moving coil: linear scale, accurate, low consumption; but d.c. only, costly and delicate. Multiplier = 100/0.002 - 50 = 49950 ohms in series; shunt = 0.1/4.998 = 0.02 ohms in parallel.

questions.stem:
(a) State three reasons for earthing an electrical installation. [3 marks]
(b) Describe the earth-rod (earth electrode) method of earthing a domestic installation. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the meaning of earth loop impedance and why it must be low. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Any three, 1 mark each: to protect people from electric shock; to ensure protective devices operate quickly on an earth fault; to maintain metalwork at earth potential; to protect against lightning/static; to stabilise system voltage
4 marks: (b) Copper or copper-clad steel rod driven vertically into moist ground (1); earthing conductor (green/yellow) clamped to the rod with a clamp/label (1); conductor run to the main earthing terminal in the consumer unit (1); earth electrode resistance tested and pit protected/kept moist (1)
2 marks: (c) Earth loop impedance is the total impedance of the path taken by fault current: from the fault through the protective conductor, earth return, supply transformer winding and phase conductor back to the fault
1 mark: (c) It must be low so that a large enough fault current flows to operate the fuse or circuit breaker quickly
questions.explanation: Earthing protects against shock, makes protective devices operate, keeps metalwork at zero potential and helps with lightning. An earth rod is driven into moist ground and connected by a green/yellow conductor to the main earthing terminal. Earth loop impedance is the impedance of the whole fault-current path; it must be low so the protective device trips quickly.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how a rotating magnetic field causes the rotor of a three-phase induction motor to turn. [4 marks]
(b) State three methods of starting three-phase induction motors. [3 marks]
(c) A 4-pole, 50 Hz induction motor runs with a slip of 3%. Calculate its rotor speed. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Three-phase currents in the stator windings produce a magnetic field rotating at synchronous speed (1); the field cuts the rotor conductors and induces e.m.f. (Faraday) (1); induced currents flow in the closed rotor circuit (1); interaction of rotor currents with the field produces torque, so the rotor turns in the direction of the field but slightly slower (1)
3 marks: (b) 1 mark each: direct-on-line (DOL); star-delta starter; auto-transformer starter (also rotor resistance for slip-ring motors)
1 mark: (c) Synchronous speed Ns = 120f/p = 120 x 50/4 = 1500 rev/min
2 marks: (c) Rotor speed = Ns(1 - s) = 1500 x 0.97 = 1455 rev/min
questions.explanation: The stator's three-phase currents create a rotating field that induces rotor currents; the resulting force turns the rotor slightly slower than synchronous speed. Starting: DOL, star-delta, auto-transformer. Ns = 1500 rev/min, rotor = 1500 x 0.97 = 1455 rev/min.
